The complete submitted proof is correct under the expressly accepted prerequisites. Eleven sequential checks verify 68 deductions, and six reference/dependency checks confirm the cited scopes and definitions. All named prerequisite reports are available and passed; earlier conditional dependencies in the intrinsic and curve reports are now resolved. No critical error or gap was found. The book was read without modification.

The modification pullback lemma is valid. L1 convergence bounds the suprema above and below; surjectivity preserves them. A common smooth curvature lower bound gives relative L1 compactness upstairs. Change of variables identifies every cluster limit on the biholomorphic locus, and the exceptional analytic set has zero smooth volume. Uniqueness of the cluster limit proves convergence of the entire pulled-back sequence.

The majorant uses one normalized subsequence on Y. For each subsequently fixed compact modification, the lemma applies to that same subsequence. Local semicontinuity has exactly the required direction: nu(limit,z) >= limsup nu(approximant,z). Pointwise Lelong numbers dominate the generic ideal order divided by m, whose subsequential limit is tau(E). Taking generic values therefore proves all compact divisorial inequalities simultaneously, without any further extraction or globalization of local modifications.

The envelope family is nonempty, bounded above and stable under finite maxima. Choquet extraction produces an increasing sequence with a genuine integrable lower barrier, hence an L1 limit equal to its canonical envelope. Pullback convergence and local semicontinuity retain every inequality. Thus T belongs to the family and is its largest member. For fixed Omega, the family is independent of the extracted majorant. Larger trace data shrink the family; larger backgrounds in the pointwise order of forms enlarge it.

The accepted Hermitian I-projection preserves every positive-weight multiplier ideal. Its local valuative consequence applies to each given compact modification and preserves the required Lelong numbers. Hence Q[T] is a trace competitor, proving Q[T]=T by maximality; the accepted P[Q]=Q identity gives P[T]=T. The original v supplies a genuine P_{Omega/2}(T). Since Omega is Hermitian, the semipositive big contact estimate gives the displayed finite measure bound. The separate smaller-background individual-positivity result gives strictly positive mass even if v_-(Omega)=0. Neither conclusion uses BMP or PVP.

The PDE corollary meets both exact clauses of the accepted ordinary-type model condition, with epsilon=1/2. The density hypotheses match thm:als-prescribed-lp. It yields the stated unique positive-exponent solution and zero-exponent existence with uniqueness of the positive scalar only.

On the curve, the atom inequalities imply positivity of the full curvature measure minus the finite atomic measure D_u. The L1 difference a-w consequently has a canonical genuine quasi-psh representative bounded above. Canonical equality extends a=w+(a-w) across poles, giving a preceq w; the converse follows from Lelong monotonicity. Thus the normalized competitor families coincide and T=P[w]. Accepted curve I-goodness in this same A eta background gives P[w]=Q[w], and projection preserves the exact curve Lelong numbers. No ordinary equivalence T~w or exact higher-dimensional realization is inferred.

The required arXiv searches returned unrelated statements. Web fallback and the supplied source verified the local Lelong facts and the matching multiplier-ideal envelope and I-goodness definitions.
